newsitem.title: BAHRAIN: Bahrain jails 11 for arson attacks.
newsitem.headline: Bahrain jails 11 for arson attacks.

text.p: Bahrain's State Security Court jailed 11 Bahrainis for three to 15 years on charges of arson attacks, newspapers said on Sunday.
They said the court on Saturday jailed two people for 15 years each for a deadly arson attack on two stores in a Bahraini village last year. A third suspect was jailed for 10 years.
An Asian was killed when attackers torched a photo studio and a spare parts shop in Nuwaidrat village, 10 km (six miles) south of the capital Manama last September.
Newspapers said the court also sentenced eight people for three to 10 years on charges of arson attacks on three power sub-stations and a water drainage pumping plant.
The defendants, who were together fined 37,100 dinars ($100,000), were also charged with an attack on a house in the Shi'ite village of Karana, six km (four miles) west of Manama.

The court, whose verdicts cannot be appealed, has jailed more than 180 people since the government, seeking to speed up judgments, last March ordered it to try hundreds of detainees held for street protests, sabotage and arson attacks.
Newspapers also said Bahrain had arrested four people on charges of a deadly arson attack on December 31 in the Shi'ite village of Tubli, eight km (five miles) south of Manama.
They quoted a Bahraini security official as saying the four had confessed to the attack in which an Asian man was killed and two were injured.

Around 28 people have been killed in more than two years of sporadic protests by members of Bahrain's majority Shi'ite Moslem community seeking political and economic reforms from the Sunni-led government.
